answer: Each epoch a verifiable random function draws every agent's grading panel from the whole pool, so no fixed jury forms. Like light through a prism, reputation refracts at each vertex of the panel network; trust emerges only from averaging many independent panels, so planted judges cannot bend it. Attackers must control much of the pool and keep fakes alive across epochs, paying entry stakes and slashing risk while payoff per sybil shrinks to zero. A plume of disposable identities evaporates: trust is re-earned under new judges each epoch.
